clue.text: Servant attending queen, maybe in ceremony

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so one piece sits right beside the other

parts.note: a page is a boy servant or attendant
a queen is one kind of ant, the egg-laying female of the colony

explanation.surface: A royal servant waits on the queen during some grand court ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'queen' a monarch, but the 'maybe' flags an example: an ant colony has a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a grand public show or procession put on as an elaborate ceremony.

clue.text: Dandy holding another up in exit

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the result is read bottom to top
holding means one copy contains the other

parts.note: a fop is a dandy
another dandy, so the same word again

explanation.surface: One dandy is holding another up in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts FOP inside FOP after its F to give FFOPOP; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to die, and pop off is informal for dying.

clue.text: On walk lightning's ultimate risk

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so this piece comes first
ultimate means last, so the final letter of lightning's is taken

parts.note: an amble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: Going for a walk in lightning is ultimately a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S is a link, so the last letter of 'lightning' is G.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a gamble is a venture whose outcome is uncertain, a risk.

clue.text: Examination of fools, blokes blocking street

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way, so the men go in the middle of the street letters

parts.note: men are blokes

explanation.surface: An examination of idiots and men blocking a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts MEN between S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an assessment is an evaluation or test of someone's ability.

clue.text: Feature on green paint splashed about

indicators.note: paint splashed about is scattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A green surface is decorated with spattered paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests colour beside 'paint', but it is a golf green.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf putting green, a tap-in is a very short putt into the hole.

clue.text: Corrupt bishop, when caught in action

indicators.note: the bishop-and-when pair is trapped inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action or act
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A corrupt bishop is caught in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' looks like being caught red-handed, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt here is an adjective: something debased has been lowered in quality or morally degraded.

clue.text: Tear apart or show contempt for someone in the club?

parts.note: to dis is slang for showing disrespect
a member belongs to a club

explanation.surface: Ripping someone apart, or snubbing a fellow club member.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut a body apart limb from limb.

clue.text: In the vicinity, avoiding a fight

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so the letter is left out

parts.note: about means nearby, in the vicinity

explanation.surface: Staying out of a scrap that is happening nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a boxing or wrestling contest.

clue.text: Extends message, suggesting only honest communication?

definitions.meaning: draws out or prolongs, as in making a meeting last
read as '...', a declaration that spin, misleading presentation, is gone

explanation.surface: Someone stretches out a speech claiming only honest talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin is the PR habit of slanting the truth; with it 'out', only plain honesty remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin something out is to make it last longer than needed, so it extends it.

clue.text: Engagement in the air?

parts.note: an engagement here is a battle, and one fought in the sky is aerial combat between fighter planes

explanation.surface: An engagement hinted at as romance is in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' and 'in the air' suggest a betrothal in the offing; it is a military engagement fought by aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-range battle between fighter aircraft is the classic aerial combat.

clue.text: Young dogs chewing the end of bedroom foot attire

indicators.note: puppies chewing something have it in their mouths, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: puppies are pups

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Puppies chewing the end of someone's bedroom slippers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing' puts M, the last letter of 'bedroom', inside PUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: pumps are light shoes, so they are a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Feeble person taken aback by mathematician showing off

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side
taken aback suggests something turned backwards, so that word is reversed

parts.note: a sop is a weak, spineless person
Alan Turing, the British mathematician and codebreaker

explanation.surface: A weakling is startled by a mathematician who is showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reads as startled, but here it turns the weakling word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Posturing is behaving in an affected way to impress, which is showing off.

clue.text: Entertainer looks disheartened, confused, when grabbed by tot

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are held inside the word for a measure of drink

parts.note: a tot or finger is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: confused means the remaining letters are jumbled
losing its heart means the middle letter of the word looks is removed

explanation.surface: A performer looks dispirited and muddled when a small child grabs hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler but is a drink measure; 'disheartened' removes the middle letter before 'confused' jumbles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a singer of traditional ballads is one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Drink — twice it gets knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: two meanings of it: the word itself, IT, and SA, sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone's drink keeps getting knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is used twice, once as IT and once as SA (sex appeal, an old slang sense of 'it'); 'gets knocked over' reverses ITSA.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Urge seizing philosopher, left asking for nothing

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the urge word wraps around the others

parts.note: to press is to urge
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: An urge grips a thinker who is left wanting nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Ayer, the logical positivist, is a crossword favourite for 'philosopher'; 'seizing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never prays makes no requests to God, so asks for nothing.

clue.text: In general, sedimentary material with nasty smell and coarse

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces are joined

parts.note: marl is a clay-and-lime sedimentary deposit
BO is body odour
rough means coarse

explanation.surface: Speaking generally, sediment that is smelly and rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'generally', but 'general' is the definition. John Churchill, Duke of Marlborough, was a great British general.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Marlborough was a famous English military commander, victor at Blenheim.

clue.text: Put new money into political party — get clear about that

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: get means receive, so the word for clear takes the party inside

parts.note: fine means clear, as of weather
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Funding a political party and coming clean about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' signals the container: the word for clear gets the party inside it, while 'about' gives the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To refinance is to provide fresh funding, often by replacing existing loans.

clue.text: Like a broader smile from son that is held in acclaim

indicators.note: held in means contained, so these letters go inside the acclaim word

parts.note: a cheer is acclaim
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A son, held in high acclaim, grins all the wider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' looks like 'held in high esteem', but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheesy grin is a wide, forced smile, as when saying 'cheese' for a photo.

clue.text: Rose and Lily may be in these shops — flirts so naughty

definitions.text: Rose and Lily may be in these shops

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Two women named Rose and Lily, in shops, are such naughty flirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose and Lily look like girls' names in shops, but they are flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Florists are flower shops, where roses and lilies are on sale.

clue.text: Ambassador frequently flanked by two chaps who launched ships?

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: flanked by means the two names stand either side of the word for often

parts.note: Len and Roy are two men's names
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A diplomat often has two men at his sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanked by' signals that the two chaps sit either side of the word for often, after His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlowe called hers 'the face that launched a thousand ships', the Greek fleet sailing to Troy.

clue.text: Roofless London theatre in the old city

indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter is the roof, so it is taken off

parts.note: the Adelphi is a theatre on the Strand in London's West End

explanation.surface: A London theatre with no roof, found in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the ancient Greek city famous for its oracle of Apollo.

clue.text: Lager girl?

definitions.meaning: ... Artois is a Belgian beer brand

explanation.definitionFit: Stella Artois is a well-known lager, and Stella is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Jewish scribe, character finally appearing in time

indicators.note: the letter shows up inside the word for a period

parts.note: an era is a period of time
the final character of the alphabet is Z

explanation.surface: A Jewish scribe's character is finally revealed in due time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character finally' looks like the last letter of 'character', but it means the last letter of the alphabet; 'appearing in' puts it inside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra was the priest and scribe who led Jews back from Babylon in the Old Testament.

clue.text: What's expressed primarily by tender man, rambling?

definitions.text: What's expressed primarily by tender man, rambling?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side
primarily means first, so the initial letter of expressed is used
rambling means wandering about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted man, wandering in his speech, utters sweet nothings.
explanation.walkthrough: E, from 'primarily', then 'rambling' shuffles TENDER MAN into NDEARMENT. The whole clue also describes what a tender man says.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving words such as darling are what a tender man would say.

clue.text: Poem, say, inscribed in cathedral

indicators.note: inscribed in means written within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Ely, a city in Cambridgeshire, England, is known for its cathedral
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A poem, for example, carved into a cathedral wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, an English city, is the crossword's standard 'cathedral'; 'inscribed in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, typically a lament for someone dead.

clue.text: PC 49, plus one in enclosed space

indicators.note: in means inside, so the Roman fifty goes within the compartment word

parts.note: a pod is an enclosed compartment
49 plus one is 50, which is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: PC 49, plus one more, in a cramped space.
explanation.walkthrough: PC 49 was a BBC radio police detective; Plod is British slang for a police officer, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Plod is British slang for an ordinary police constable, a PC.

clue.text: At home, only once losing head, showing rudeness

parts.note: in means at home
sole means only

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes from the word once

explanation.surface: Back at home, a person who once lost their temper is behaving rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes O off ONCE to leave NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: insolence is disrespectful, cheeky behaviour, a form of rudeness.

clue.text: Put out of school, former student lurks outside gym

indicators.note: the former-student pair waits around the gym letters, enclosing them

parts.note: ex means former
L, for learner, stands for a student
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: An old boy is expelled after loitering outside the school gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lurks outside' signals the container: the former student wraps around the gym letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to throw a pupil out of school permanently.

clue.text: Author in hurry to disappear? Yes, once!

parts.note: rush means hurry
to die is to pass away, vanishing from the world

explanation.surface: An author in a hurry to vanish, and he once really did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes, once!' is a comment: Salman Rushdie had to go into hiding after the 1989 fatwa.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is the novelist who wrote Midnight's Children and The Satanic Verses.

clue.text: Positive greeting meets Virginia in school

indicators.note: meets means joins up with, so the pieces are placed together

parts.note: yes is a positive answer
hi is a greeting
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A cheerful hello greets a Virginian at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeshiva is an Orthodox Jewish college for studying the Talmud.
